# Full audit

## The task

<!-- Is the ground truth correct? Is each item well described, with one defensible answer?
Is it solvable as given, with what the agent is actually allowed? Can the answer be reached
without doing the task: from the environment, by guessing, from memory? One literal example
item. Cite items by id. -->

## The grader

<!-- Does it credit only correct answers? Does it reject correct ones? Is it stable:
deterministic, the same judge across the leaderboard, reproducible today? Does it capture
what the task is for, or a proxy? Name the judge model(s) actually recorded in the logs. -->

## The harness and environment

<!-- Configured as the paper and code say (versions, tools, network, data present)? Fair
across models (same tools, budgets, prompts, termination)? Any leak that should not be
there: web access, stale state, answer files? Did the environment break attempts? -->

## Aggregation and limits

<!-- What was excluded before the headline number, and why? Do turn, token or time limits
cut off capable work, unequally across models? Is the number informative: saturation,
a ceiling from broken items, statistical power? Attempted and completed populations. -->

## How agents approach it

<!-- Where do they converge, diverge, get confused? Does behaviour disagree with the paper's
account? Label the failed attempts: capability failure, or one of the causes above, with
counts per model and denominators. -->

## How it is built

<!-- Code quality of task, scorer and harness; divergence between paper, README and
implementation; things a maintainer should fix. Low weight; keep it short. -->
